title: Ancho-Tilapia with Charred Corn Salsa
seoTitle: Ancho-Tilapia with Charred Corn Salsa | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Tilapia grill night—chili lime char, corn salsa, fast crew portions
subtitle: Cilantro-chili lime tilapia, charred corn salsa, and ten portions
description: Tilapia fillets marinate in chili-lime-cilantro paste, grill on oiled grates until 145°F, and serve with charred corn-black bean salsa.

steps.title: Build chili lime paste
steps.instruction: Blend lime juice, ancho powder, chipotle, half the cilantro, garlic, and salt into a paste. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Marinate tilapia
steps.instruction: Coat fillets in paste. Marinate 20 minutes refrigerated only—acid toughens longer soaks. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Char corn for salsa
steps.instruction: Grill corn at 425°F until charred. Cut kernels off cob. Toss with beans, onion, lime, and remaining cilantro. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Preheat grill grates
steps.instruction: Preheat grill to medium-high, 400°F. Oil grates generously. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Grill tilapia
steps.instruction: Grill fillets 3–4 minutes per side until charred and 145°F internal. Use fish spatula—tilapia is fragile. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest before plating
steps.instruction: Rest fillets 2 minutes. Transfer to hotel pans. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold at 140°F
steps.instruction: Hold covered at 140°F up to 10 minutes max. Add avocado to salsa at service. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Platter for ten
steps.instruction: Serve one fillet per firefighter with corn-black bean salsa and avocado. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: 20-minute marinade max—lime turns tilapia mushy if over-soaked.
Oiled grates and fish spatula prevent fillet crumble.
Avocado in salsa at the line, not during hold.
tonightSpread: Chili lime grilled tilapia with charred corn salsa.
leftovers: Flake tilapia into fish tacos with extra salsa.
Chop into tortilla soup with lime.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Tilapia is budget-friendly and cooks in minutes. Chili-lime flavor is distinct from catfish remoulade or trout glaze—holds at 140°F briefly on platters.
mealPrepNotes: Marinate fillets 20 minutes max. Grill medium-high 400°F, 3–4 minutes per side. Hold covered at 140°F up to 10 minutes. Salsa at room temp.
